question: Nitin bought some sharpeners at the rate of ₹180/dozen. He sold them for ₹20 each. His profit percentage is ______% (rounded off to two decimal places).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Cost Price to Selling Price for 1 dozen items = 180 : (12 × 20) = 180 : 240 = 3 : 4

Profit = 4 − 3 = 1 unit on a base of 3 units.

Profit % = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 = 33.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of 1 dozen (12 sharpeners) = ₹180

Selling price of 1 sharpener = ₹20

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 CP of 1 dozen
 ₹180

 SP of 1 dozen
 ₹240

 Profit % = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100
 SP of 1 dozen = 12 × ₹20 = ₹240

**Calculations:**

⇒ Selling Price (SP) of 1 dozen (12 sharpeners) = 12 × 20 = ₹240

⇒ Cost Price (CP) of 1 dozen = ₹180

⇒ Profit = 240 − 180 = ₹60

⇒ Profit % = (60 ÷ 180) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 = 33.33%

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is given on Marked Price (MP) to arrive at Selling Price (SP). Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer claims to sell at Cost Price but uses false weight, Profit % = (Error ÷ True Weight − Error) × 100.

Successive Percentage Change

When there are multiple profit/loss changes, the net effect can be calculated as [a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100]%, where loss is negative.
